avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, control of the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and it pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: money from the parks fund, equipment rentals, blue-collar worker crews. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant installation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report no later than December 31, 2026, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks
etapes.texte: Several boroughs are renting sweeper trucks, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives after winter. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve is authorizing an expenditure of $574,920.99, taxes included, for four sweeper trucks and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is contracting companies for the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough is also extending snow removal in the Quartier des Spectacles for one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

Montréal-Nord is paying for an additional rented grader during the 2025-2026 winter, and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 in surplus to its 2026 snow removal operations, after 39 abrasive spreadings since November 15, 2025, while the budget had planned for 20. The City and several boroughs are extending by 12 months turnkey snow removal, towing and equipment rental with operators contracts.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at parks and buildings
etapes.texte: The City is extending snow removal for the parking lot of the édifice Jacinthe-Fyfe and for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the Montréal soccer stadium. It is also awarding a contract for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal services in the Grand parc de l'Ouest cover two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031, with each season running from November 1 to April 15.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and paying for the day-to-day operation of this plant. Boroughs are taking charge of replacing lead water service lines, including the portion located on private land.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without digging a trench, and to redo the roadway in various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include replacing lead water service connections on the public side and the private side.

etapes.titre: Lead water service lines on private land
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering city council the chance to take charge of replacing lead service lines located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and is adding funds to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the work replaces a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemicals, residue landfilling, cleaning, upgrading the sludge incinerators and mechanical work. The mechanical work is aimed in particular at reconditioning bar screens damaged during heavy rains [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption planned for October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite planned to run until December 2027; the ozone plant is scheduled to come into service in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward several projects at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain around the park. It is also asking the Québec government for money for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.titre: Request for funding for the footbridge
etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre path through the park, including a footbridge of about 150 metres, and assistance of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project over to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The borough then awards a contract of $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract of $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work covers a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract of up to $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, the water main, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City awards two companies the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It also extends the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium by six months, for an additional $193,215.49, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex by five months, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included; the compost is used in part to develop the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes the submission of a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is submitting its request, closes on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, additional mortar, sodded turf, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application does not involve any spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, upgrading its light fixtures to meet standards, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération [Register of natural environments protected and contributing to biodiversity in the urban agglomeration], with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Reconstruction of the chemin Senneville culvert
etapes.texte: A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow clearing, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the contract for snow clearing of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the contract for cleaning nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other declining trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow clearing of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and declining trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan to be filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the uncharged rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre over the winter of 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain St-Denis fit-out
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose the project funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fit-out work of the temporary warming centre at Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal of ruling
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City is approving the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM, transferring or buying land for social housing, and giving grants to organizations that build affordable housing. It is also amending the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units [CM26 0114]. City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the 2026 budget of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households [CG26 0024].

The City accepts, free of charge, half the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre lot on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, from the Government of Canada [CG26 0042]. It also transfers, at no cost, a 789.6 square-metre lot at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni, where the co-op must build 26 housing units [CG26 0062].

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [CG26 0171]. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project [CG26 0178].

etapes.titre: Land purchase and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City buys a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre lot near rue Chatham and rue William, in the Sud-Ouest, for $9,293,113, plus taxes, for social housing purposes [CG26 0286]. It removes the right of first refusal for social housing on lots in Ville-Marie and the Sud-Ouest that have been covered since 2020 [CG26 0292].

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus [CG26 0372] and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in Pointe-Saint-Charles [CG26 0559]. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build 72 housing units on 2e Avenue [CE26 1028], and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a policy to refund 50% of permit fees for eligible projects [CA26 170209].

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 housing units at Technopôle Angus by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Delivery of the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue in May 2028.
Occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles in February 2030.
Inclusion of the fee exemption in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce's 2027 local fee by-law.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square-metre lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square-metre lot to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités", because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and the soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, water main, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 taxes included, and a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the remediation of the soil at the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net through the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a complex of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor space index of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of a financial assistance application to the Ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks of this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine lease runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is on loan until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade lot from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public spaces in the eco-district remain to be named before the development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for citizens. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, each for six months, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transshipped in Montréal-Est, then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchases and sorting equipment loans
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to provide collection bins to citizens of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration is extending the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from the ecocentres, assigning two firms to conduct studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extending the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The dishware, water fountain and sorting station loan program is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an extension from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for the water mains and public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline extended to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Government of Québec grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the former racetrack site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension involves no financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water mains, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and recreation centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector.

The City is leasing parcels of the site to community cafeteria MultiCaf and Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a nominal rent, and the organizations pay for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Government of Québec to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on infrastructure being completed by 2031; the credits from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the deed of transfer to complete at least one building, and the affordability of the housing must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and renovation of parks across the island: work contracts, soil studies, public art and adjustments to projects already underway. Several projects come from Montréal's participatory budget or from boroughs' dedicated park funds. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, the City is awarding maintenance and work contracts, and is submitting an application for an international designation on night lighting.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are awarding contracts to redo play areas, water play features, paths and dog parks: parc Lucie-Bruneau in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King, parc Alexis-Nihon, parc Monseigneur-Langlois, parc Denise-Morelle. Outremont is paying $150,000 to the school service centre to redo the play structure at parc-école Saint-Germain.

etapes.titre: Work and maintenance in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for renovating the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and is awarding the reconstruction of a culvert under that same road, at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It is also awarding contracts for snow removal on service roads, felling of ash trees and dying trees, and janitorial maintenance of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for DarkSky International's Urban Night Sky Place international designation. It is adding the parc-nature des Sources and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité.

The City is adding amounts or shifting budgets within contracts already awarded: construction monitoring for parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parc des Hirondelles, parc du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray and parc Percy-Walters. It is also converting an 810.2 m² lot from the former rue Eadie, at parc Campbell Ouest, into a local park.

aSurveiller.texte: Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan to be submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, site compliance work by April 2032.
Public art at parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner selected in October 2026, contract in December 2026, artwork installed in 2028.
Parc Le Prévost: transfer of the lane strip to public ownership as a local park to go before the executive committee on October 7, 2026 and city council on October 19, 2026.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027, after the warranty year.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and overseeing temporary pedestrian streets on commercial thoroughfares, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial thoroughfares [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the by-laws that close the streets, authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot and official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by by-law [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to the public square works at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee allocates $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their thoroughfares to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street status (public square) to local park status [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite » [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting an additional six months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, a date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The Ville de Montréal's Police Department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The city awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for people detained by the SPVM, and extends by one year the maintenance of the computer-aided dispatch system software with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease of the training centre in Anjou and that of neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

The city enters into an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9 mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends by one year the SPVM's courier contract, and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and loans a detective sergeant to the Sûreté du Québec team on exporting stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" (baked beans) day of the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the Anjou borough purchased 62 tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer.
March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis, and ACCEF committees.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the Société de transport de Montréal (STM)'s 2026 budget and capital program, then a series of STM loan by-laws. It sells, leases or lends land to the STM for entrances, ventilation plants and parking. It also oversees construction sites around the network and awards mandates related to the Blue Line extension.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council tables then approves the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in revenues and expenses, and its 2026-2035 capital program [CG26 0022]. The City also enters into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel [CG26 0064].

etapes.titre: Construction sites overseen around the network
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville modifies bus waiting areas as part of the network redesign [CA26 09 0020], Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the green line tunnel vault 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026 [CA26 240269], and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at bus stops [CA26 08 0373]. The City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation plant in Outremont [CM26 0198], does not oppose the reconstruction of a tunnel bridge over the REM [CG26 0379] and adds $250,000 of related work to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, to be billed to the STM [CG26 0526].

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 [CG26 0175]. It then enters into framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design and impact management of the Blue Line corridor redevelopment [CG26 0564], and city council adopts a motion asking Québec to study preserving the tunnel boring machine « Lisette » [CM26 0920].

The City purchases advertising space in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 [CG26 0164], and pays $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships [CG26 0461]. The borough councils of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle adopt motions calling for structuring public transit in the East and in the Greater Southwest.

The agglomeration approves several STM loans and the corresponding changes to the 2026-2035 capital program: analysis of replacing the MR-73 cars [CG26 0393], extending their service life [CG26 0504], bus priority measures [CG26 0500], Réno-Infrastructures phase 4 raised to $640,000,000 [CG26 0501], surface infrastructure repairs [CG26 0506] and technological and security risk management [CG26 0503].

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lot runs for three years starting October 1, 2026, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
The agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée cover 72 months, from October 2026 to October 2032.
The repair and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation plant, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer vacation, for the reconstruction of the tunnel bridge.
The opening of the five new Blue Line extension stations is planned for 2031.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the BIXI bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI bike-share system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new cycling construction projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an order that officially establishes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse and imposes mandatory manoeuvres on motorists up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including the repair of the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

City council authorized the submission of four funding applications to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete funding applications to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between the west side of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
